description: Repair and resume greedy nearest positional scalar unions
proposal: Family: parameter tying. Current retained frontier is 2,105 parameters at 99.050000%, a +0.050000 percentage-point margin over 99%. There have been 18 prior attempts in this family. The most recent accepted result is attempt-0074 at 2,105 parameters and 99.05%; the most recent failed result is attempt-0075, whose only micro-trial was an implementation error before training because the helper removed a required closing parenthesis. This is the permitted repair of that reproducible implementation error: the source splice now retains the existing pair close, while the intended candidate and conditions are otherwise unchanged. Hypothesis: parameterization-preserving unions of the closest learned positional scalar groups can continue reducing count without losing qualification. Ordering is ascending absolute group-value difference, excluding exact rejected pairs; this is more informative than the nearest untested alternative because each selected pair is the minimum-distortion eligible union. The official runner alone accepts or rolls back each one-pair candidate. Stop after 20 micro-trials, immediately on any further execution error, or if no pair remains. Compute budget: at most 20 migrations and official verifications, 30 minutes wall-clock.
summary: Completed the declared 20 nearest-group positional unions in 20 minutes 53 seconds. All 20 micro-trials qualified and were retained; 0 discards and 0 errors. The frontier moved from 2,105 parameters at 99.05% to 2,085 parameters at 99.04%. Pairwise value differences rose from 4.198e-6 to 1.285e-5; stop reason was the fixed 20-micro-trial cap. Training used checkpoint migration rather than fresh optimization, followed by 20 official verifications.
